summary.prose: A turn now says which documents to show for review by calling a new insrc_present tool with their ids, and the chat opens exactly those in the review pane. The chat reads the declaration from the tool call's own small input, not from any tool result, so a large result that the CLI shortens can no longer make a review document fail to open. Both providers are covered: the Claude tool_use input and the Codex mcp_tool_call arguments, whose shape was captured from a real Codex run and is pinned as a fixture. The old reading of tool output and the end-of-turn guess are removed, a name that is not pending is reported in the chat and to the controller, and the steering tells the controller to declare what it presents.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Declare the documents a turn presents instead of parsing tool output

dataModelChanges.details: The tool-call turn event gains an optional present list, set by the provider mappers from the input of the insrc_present MCP tool only. It is live-only and is not written to the transcript, so stored rows and old sessions are unchanged. The review presenter's turn handle changes from reading tool results and the end of the turn to receiving a declared list; the chat host feeds it from the tool-call event. The MCP server registers the new insrc_present tool, its input schema is added to the schema registry, and the steering block, the steering template and the guide's approval text are rewritten to tell the controller to call it. Codex: a real capture (codex-cli 0.162.1, pinned as vscode-plugin/src/chat/__tests__/fixtures/codex-mcp-tool-call.jsonl) shows an MCP call as an item of type mcp_tool_call with server, tool (a bare name, not server-qualified), arguments (a JSON object) and status, emitted on item.started and again on item.completed. The Codex mapper in cli-adapter.ts, which today handles only command_execution and tool_call items on item.completed, gains a branch for mcp_tool_call on item.completed only, matches tool equal to insrc_present, reads arguments.documents as an array of strings (no JSON-string form is accepted, since none was observed) and sets present; started items are ignored so the call declares once, and a failed completed item still declares. It also sets the event's mcp field from server and tool, which that mapper never set before. Registering insrc_present also changes the schema registry's expected tool list and the steering skeleton's tool catalog, which schema-registry.test.ts pins, so that list and the catalog row are updated in the same commit; the CLAUDE.md copies of the steering block are refreshed by repo.add and are not edited by hand. The MCP tool surface is pinned by a golden fixture: forward-step.test.ts asserts the tool list against tool-surface.golden.json, so insrc_present is inserted into the fixture in name-sorted position, between insrc_guide and insrc_review_step, because forward-step.test.ts compares the sorted live surface to the golden list index by index, the count rises to thirteen (the 'twelve tools' test title and the length check of 12 in forward-step.test.ts are updated), and schema-registry.test.ts's EXPECTED_TOOLS and PHASELESS_TOOLS are updated. The MCP-side handler needs a new unary workflow.pending wrapper in daemon-stream.ts (none exists), and the chat's pending lookup in docs-review-client.ts is reused as it is: it already drops records with no document file. The chat host passes a declaration from both of its feed paths, the followed live turn and the hosted run. The existing presenter and chat-panel tests that pin toolResult and the end-of-turn open are rewritten to the declared contract, and steering-template.md only points at the steering block, so the approval text changes in steering-block.md and the guide.

migration.stateBefore: The review presenter infers what to open: it JSON-parses each tool result for a top-level pendingApproval.artifactPath, and at the end of a turn it opens whatever became pending since the turn began. The Claude CLI replaces an oversized MCP result with a non-JSON preview, so a large workflow result opens nothing, and the end-of-turn guess depends on a pending list that holds hundreds of old records. The tool-call turn event carries no input, and the Codex mapper handles only command_execution and tool_call items, so a Codex mcp_tool_call item falls through unmapped (review-presenter.ts, chat-panel.ts, stream-events.ts and cli-adapter.ts, from the s1 bundles).
migration.stateAfter: The controller declares what it presents by calling a new insrc_present tool, whose input names the documents. Each provider mapper puts that list on the tool-call turn event (Claude from the tool_use input; Codex from the arguments object of a completed mcp_tool_call item, in the shape captured from codex-cli 0.162.1), the chat host hands it to the presenter, and the presenter opens exactly those pending documents once each, reporting any name that is not pending. The presenter no longer reads tool results or guesses at the end of a turn, and the steering text, the steering template and the guide tell the controller to declare before it asks for approval.

migrationSteps.action: Add the insrc_present MCP tool with its input schema and its answer of presented and notPending, validated against the daemon's pending list; it changes nothing and can ship before anything calls it, and update the schema registry's expected tool list in schema-registry.test.ts and the steering skeleton's tool catalog row, the golden tool-surface fixture and its count in forward-step.test.ts, and PHASELESS_TOOLS; the tool's handler runs MCP-side and reads the pending list through the workflow.pending IPC for the resolved repo, with a new workflow.pending wrapper in daemon-stream.ts for its handler

Extend the tool-call turn event with the optional present list and set it in the provider mappers from the insrc_present input only, live-only: the Claude mapper from the tool_use input, and the Codex mapper from the completed mcp_tool_call item's arguments object, with the real capture pinned as a fixture and tested

Change the presenter's turn handle to take a declared list and open exactly those pending documents once each, with a not-pending report that the chat shows as a line; feed it from the tool-call event in the chat host

Rewrite the steering block, the steering template and the guide's approval text to tell the controller to call insrc_present before it asks for approval, and to give the document's path in its message as well
Remove presentedPathOf, the reading of tool results and the end-of-turn guess, with the tests that pinned them, only after the steps above are in

migration.backwardCompat: The MCP tool is additive and the turn event field is optional, so an older plugin shows an insrc_present call as an ordinary tool row and keeps its old behaviour until it is updated, and an older daemon without the tool simply lacks it. The daemon (which serves the MCP tools) should be updated before the plugin that stops reading tool results, or the controller would have no tool to call. Stored transcript rows and old sessions are unaffected.

alternativesConsidered.name: A dedicated present tool whose input names the documents
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: The controller calls insrc_present with the documents to open; the chat reads that call's small input from the turn event and opens exactly those.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Add one MCP tool, insrc_present, taking a list of artifact ids or document paths. The controller calls it whenever it asks the user to review or approve something. The tool validates the names against the daemon's pending list and returns a short result naming any that are not pending. The chat host reads the declaration from the turn's tool-call event, which is extended to carry the declared documents for this tool only (read by each provider mapper from the call's input: the Claude tool_use input, or the arguments object of a Codex mcp_tool_call item), resolves each name through the pending list and opens it quietly in the review pane. A name that does not resolve is shown in the chat as a line, not guessed at. The old parsing of tool output and the end-of-turn guess are removed, and the steering text and guide tell the controller to call insrc_present before asking for approval.
pros: The contract is explicit and sits in the turn's own tool call, with a tiny input that no result truncation can touch
One new tool and one small event extension, with no change to every other tool
The tool can answer the controller at once if a document is not pending, so a mistake is visible to both the controller and the user
Both providers expose the call's input on the stream, verified live for Codex
cons: The controller must remember to call it, so the steering has to say so and a missing call means nothing opens
Adds a declared-documents field to the turn event for one tool

alternativesConsidered.name: A present field on every workflow and review tool
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Each existing insrc tool takes an optional present list in its input, and the chat reads it from that call.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Add an optional present field (artifact ids or paths) to the inputs of insrc_workflow_step, insrc_build_step, insrc_review_step, insrc_code_review_step and the others that end in an approval. The chat reads the field from each tool-call event's input. The field is declared in each tool's schema and the steering says to set it on the call that produces a document for approval.
pros: The declaration rides on the call that creates the document, so no extra call
cons: Eight or more schemas change, and every new tool must remember the field
The document does not exist yet when the call is made (the call is what creates it), so the name cannot be checked against the pending list at declaration time
Larger tool-call inputs for tools that already carry big payloads
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Also explicit, but it changes eight or more schemas, and the document does not exist yet when the declaring call is made, so the name cannot be validated then.

alternativesConsidered.name: The daemon records what each tool presents and the chat follows it
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: The tools register presented documents with the daemon, and the chat reads that record, with no controller declaration.
alternativesConsidered.approach: When a workflow, build or review tool writes a document for approval, the daemon records it as presented in a small ledger. The chat host reads the ledger for the turn through IPC and opens what it holds. The controller declares nothing.
pros: No controller action, so nothing to forget
Independent of the CLI's result handling
cons: It is not an explicit contract in the turn: the chat still infers what to open, now from the daemon's record
A new daemon ledger and an IPC for it, plus rules for when an entry expires
It would open documents the controller did not mean to show the user
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: It removes the controller's declaration, which is the point of the request: the chat would still infer what to open, now from a daemon ledger, and could open what was not meant to be shown.
